I write my name on the paper.
This café has a pretty name.

explain_en: For elders, use the honorific 성함 instead of 이름: 성함이 어떻게 되세요? ('May I ask your name?'). Korean names put the family name (Kim, Lee, Park) first. Calling someone by given name alone is only for close relationships.

en: I am sorry; excuse me (polite apology)

examples.en: Excuse me, are you Haruka?
Excuse me, that's my seat.
Oh, I'm sorry. Are you okay?

examples.ko: 죄송합니다. 저는 이 가게 직원이 아니에요.
examples.en: Sorry, I don't work in this shop.
I'm sorry. I don't know Korean well.

explain: 죄송합니다는 “미안해요”보다 더 공손해요. 손님, 사장님, 모르는 사람에게 써요. 친구에게는 “미안해”라고 해요.
explain_en: 죄송합니다 is more humble than 미안해요. Use it with customers, bosses and strangers. With friends, say 미안해.

examples.en: That's okay. I'm Haruka.
It's okay. I make mistakes sometimes too.
Would you like some coffee? — No, I'm fine.
Is this seat okay?
Are you okay? Let's go to the hospital.

explain: 괜찮아요는 “문제없어요”예요. 누가 뭘 권할 때 “괜찮아요”라고 하면 “됐어요, 안 받아요”라는 뜻도 돼요.

usage: 회사원 = someone who works at a company (회사). 직장인 = anyone with a job, wider.

examples.en: My husband is an office worker.
I'm not a student. I'm an office worker.
An office worker works in an office.
Are you an office worker? — Yes, I work at a company in Seoul.
The morning subway is full of office workers.

explain: 직업을 물으면 '회사원이에요'보다 '회사 다녀요'라고 더 많이 말해요.

dict_examples.ko: 출근 시간의 지하철은 직장으로 향하는 회사원으로 늘 만원이다.
dict_examples.en: The subway at rush hour is always packed with office workers heading to work.

explain_en: When asked about their job, Koreans more often say 회사 다녀요 ('I go to a company') than 회사원이에요.

examples.en: My younger sibling is a college student.
My friend is a Korean college student.
College students take classes at university.

examples.en: I'm a college student. I'm studying Korean in Korea now.
There are a lot of college students in the library.

It's night in the US right now.

explain_en: An American can be 미국 사람 or 미국인. 인 means “person”. 미국인 is more common in news and writing.

examples.en: My older brother is a doctor.
The doctor gave me medicine.
A doctor sees patients at the hospital.
Doctor, I have a headache.
My dream is to be a doctor.

Japan is next to Korea.
I work at a Japanese company.
I'm going to Japan next week.

explain: 두 나라 이름을 짧게 합칠 때가 있어요. 한국 + 일본 = “한일”, 한국 + 중국 = “한중”이에요. 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Korean often joins two country names into a short word: 한국 + 일본 = 한일, 한국 + 중국 = 한중. You will see these in the news.

examples.en: What's your job? I'm a teacher.
I'm a nurse by profession.
Do you have a job? — Yes, I'm an office worker.
My husband's job is chef.
My friend and I have the same job.
